meta.dataset: U.S. overtime rules by state for a typical nonexempt private-sector employee
meta.coverage: 50 U.S. states (District of Columbia and territories excluded)
meta.purpose: Backend/static data for an overtime-pay calculator and 50 state SEO pages. Research output only; not legal advice.
meta.method: Primary-source-first research. Official sources: U.S. DOL WHD state table (updated 2026-07-01) cross-checked for all 50 states, plus state agencies, legislatures and courts where retrieved. Secondary sources are used only to cross-check or to flag unverified items and are listed separately.

federal_baseline.rule: 1.5x the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek for covered nonexempt employees (29 U.S.C. 207(a)(1)); no federal daily overtime, weekend/holiday premium or double time.
federal_baseline.workweek: Fixed, regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods).
federal_baseline.status: 2024 DOL salary rule vacated Nov. 15, 2024; DOL published a technical amendment on 2026-05-14 restoring the 2019 levels ($684/week; $107,432 HCE).
federal_baseline.federal_income_tax_note: One Big Beautiful Bill Act: federal income-tax deduction for 'qualified overtime compensation' for tax years 2025-2028 - only the premium ('half') portion of overtime required by the FLSA; up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint), phase-out above $150,000 ($300,000 joint) MAGI. State-only overtime (e.g., California daily overtime) is not FLSA-required. Store FLSA-required overtime hours separately from state-only overtime hours if a tax feature is added.

law_categories.flsa_baseline_no_independent_state_ot_ru: No independent state overtime rule; federal FLSA (1.5x after 40 hrs/week) is the practical baseline.
law_categories.state_threshold_higher_than_40_but_flsa_: State statute uses a higher threshold (KS 46, MN 48) but applies only where FLSA does not; use FLSA 40 for the typical case.
law_categories.state_weekly_40_rule_no_general_daily_ot: State statute also uses weekly 40 at 1.5x (no general daily overtime); may carry industry-specific wrinkles.
law_categories.state_daily_or_unusual_general_rules: State rules materially differ from a plain weekly-40 formula for a typical nonexempt worker (daily triggers etc.).

confidence_scale.High: DOL July-2026 table and at least one additional independent source (state official source/statute citation, or the NALC compilation) agree and no unresolved conflict affects the general rule.
confidence_scale.Medium: Agreement exists but a source conflict or heavy reliance on secondary material affects the rule or a material special rule.
confidence_scale.Low: Unresolved conflict on the general rule (none in this dataset).

engines.weekly_flsa: Overtime hours = max(0, total weekly hours - weekly_threshold_hours); pay at multiplier x regular rate. Used by 46 states (all except AK, CA, CO, NV).
engines.california: Daily 8/12, weekly 40, seventh-consecutive-day 8-hour rule, double time, no pyramiding (see report section 4).
engines.colorado: Greater-of of weekly >40, daily >12 and (when shift times are known) 12 consecutive hours; 1.5x only.
engines.alaska: Daily >8 plus weekly >40 where the weekly count excludes hours already paid as daily overtime.
engines.nevada: If regular rate < 1.5 x state minimum wage: greater-of daily >8 and weekly >40; otherwise weekly only.

ky_seventh_day.description: If all 7 days worked and total > 40: OT hours = max(weekly OT, seventh-day hours).

ct_restaurant_seventh_day.description: Restaurant/hotel-restaurant seventh consecutive day: premium at 1.5x the MINIMUM rate (not regular rate) per state wage order - caveat-only in MVP.

ri_sunday_holiday.description: Sunday/holiday hours at 1.5x; retail excludes those hours from the weekly count, non-retail stacks.

or_manufacturing_daily_10.description: Manufacturing/cannery/packing-plant workers: also daily OT after 10 hours (interaction with weekly under BOLI guidance must be verified).

or_ag_threshold_schedule.description: Agricultural workers: weekly threshold 48 through 2026-12-31, 40 from 2027-01-01.

universal_do_not_implement_as_default: Exempt/nonexempt classification (salary and duties tests) - the MVP assumes a nonexempt employee
Regular-rate adjustments: non-discretionary bonuses, commissions, shift differentials, piece rates, multiple pay rates
Salaried nonexempt employees (salary-to-hourly conversion, fluctuating workweek)
Compensatory time off in lieu of overtime (public sector and some states)
Collective bargaining agreements and employer policies that exceed the law
Public-sector employees and special FLSA classes (police/fire 7(k), hospital 8/80 option, motor-carrier and agricultural exemptions)
Minors and other special worker classes

scheduled_changes.change: Agricultural overtime threshold falls from 48 to 40 hours per week (HB 4002 (2022); BOLI).
Farm-laborer overtime threshold falls from 52 to 48 hours (then 44 on 2030-01-01 and 40 on 2032-01-01).
Minimum wage scheduled to reach $15.00 (affects the regular-rate floor only; overtime rule unchanged).
Daily-overtime rate threshold = 1.5 x state minimum wage; recompute whenever NRS 608.250 minimum changes ($18.00 while minimum is $12.00).

known_source_conflicts.issue: DOL table says COMPS overtime applies to four industries; CDLE INFO #1 says COMPS covers all private-sector work.
known_source_conflicts.resolution: CDLE (primary state agency) used; DOL note appears to reflect the pre-2020 Minimum Wage Order.

known_source_conflicts.issue: Agricultural overtime threshold: CDLE 2026 poster says 48 (56 at some highly seasonal sites); NALC compilation says 54/56.
Farm-worker threshold in 2026: NYSDOL says 52; a vendor page says 56; NALC compilation says 60.
Seventh-day rule scope: statute text/Labor Cabinet poster say it does not apply when the employee is not permitted to work more than 40 hours; a 2026 blog says it applies regardless of weekly hours.
known_source_conflicts.resolution: Official text used; module flagged Medium.

known_source_conflicts.issue: DOL table lists no Utah overtime provision; NALC compilation lists Utah Code 34-28-1 with a 40-hour rule.
known_source_conflicts.resolution: Treated as FLSA baseline (same 40 hrs/1.5x result); verify with Utah Labor Commission.

known_source_conflicts.issue: DOLI's 2021 flyer describes the original Virginia Overtime Wage Act; later 2022 amendment (per secondary reports) tied it to FLSA.
known_source_conflicts.resolution: Treated as FLSA baseline with a state remedy.

known_source_conflicts.issue: Reports that BOLI changed how daily (manufacturing) and weekly overtime interact (both vs greater-of).
known_source_conflicts.resolution: Manufacturing module kept optional; verify on BOLI manufacturing page.

known_source_conflicts.issue: Agricultural 48-hour rule details differ between sources (generally vs selected workweeks).
AO 2025-05 is advisory and fact-specific; AO 2025-07 on rolling/overlapping workdays was only excerpted.
known_source_conflicts.resolution: Greater-of implemented; workday approximated by entered day.

limitations: Typical nonexempt employee only; exempt status, CBAs, public-sector and industry-specific rules are excluded from defaults.
For states with no state-specific official page retrieved, the DOL WHD table is the only official source read in this research (see source audit).
State legislative sessions in 2026 were not individually reviewed for all 50 states; a broad search for 2026 overtime changes found none that alter the rules below beyond those flagged.
Word/PDF originals of some rules (e.g., COMPS Order #40) could not be parsed by the tools used; rule details were taken from agency posters/INFO documents.
Advisory opinions (e.g., Nevada AO 2025-05) are non-binding.
meta.disclaimer: Estimator data only. Not legal, tax or payroll advice. Re-verify before launch and on a recurring schedule (at least each January 1 and July 1).
meta.static_deployment_note: Designed to ship as one versioned static JSON file (no database); state lookups are by slug.

mvp_rule.logic: Enter hours for each of the 7 days of the workweek (in order). If hours are entered on all 7 days, day 7 is the 'seventh consecutive workday'. For days 1-6: reg = min(h,8); OT15 = min(max(h-8,0),4); DT = max(h-12,0). Day 7 (only if all 7 days worked): OT15 = min(h,8); DT = max(h-8,0). weekly_reg_hours = sum of reg for days 1-6; weekly_OT = max(0, weekly_reg_hours - 40) (paid 1.5x, removed from straight time). Pay = rate x (straight + 1.5 x (OT15 + weekly_OT) + 2 x DT). Ignore alternative workweek schedules (show caveat).

Exempt status (salary >= 2x state minimum wage + duties)
